To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TRIPS architecture, a new, explicit data graph execution architecture, is a promising alternative to RISC for future microprocessor designs, and that the TRIPS compiler and runtime system are capable of delivering high performance for a wide range of applications.

(1) The TRIPS architecture, a new, explicit data graph execution instruction set architecture (ISA), can be used to implement a wide class of applications, and (2) TRIPS is capable of delivering performance comparable with that of the state-of-the-art x86 ISA, but with a much lower power budget.
TRIPS is the first instantiation and proof of concept of an EDGE architecture, a new, general class of instruction set architecture that will scale to the end of Moore’s law.

the development of a new class of instruction set architecture, EDGE, which we believe is necessary to address the challenges posed by the end of silicon.
the design of a new class of architectures that are well suited to the next decade of technology scaling.

the design of new architectures and instruction set architectures that can exploit the massive integration levels of modern semiconductor technologies while scaling to the limits of power efficiency and performance.

a new ISA is necessary for future microprocessors to achieve the levels of power efficiency required for the next decade of CMOS scaling.
